title: AstraZeneca Pharma India Q1 Revenue Surges 30% to Rs 683 Crore, Rare Disease Sales Jump 35-Fold

contentHtml:
Bengaluru: AstraZeneca Pharma India Limited has reported a 30% year-on-year growth in total revenue from operations to Rs 6,828 million for the quarter ended June 30, 2026, supported by continued momentum across its core therapy areas of Oncology, Biopharmaceuticals and Rare Disease.

The company said the quarter reflected disciplined execution, key regulatory milestones and strategic partnerships aimed at expanding access to innovative healthcare solutions in India.

For the quarter, the company reported profit before exceptional item and tax of ₹510 million, while profit after exceptional item and tax stood at ₹507 million. The company clarified in its regulatory filing that the phrase “Profit after exceptional item and tax” appearing in the financial performance summary should be read as “Profit after exceptional item and before tax,” that is, profit before tax.

The Oncology segment generated ₹4,649 million, registering 26% growth compared with Q1 FY2025-26. Biopharmaceuticals, covering CVRM, R&I and V&I, recorded revenue of ₹1,619 million, reflecting 36% growth, while the Rare Diseases segment reported ₹144 million, representing 35-fold growth over the corresponding period.

Bhavana Agrawal, Chief Financial Officer and Director of AstraZeneca Pharma India, said the company delivered 30% growth in the first quarter, taking revenue to ₹6,828 million. She noted that the performance builds on the company's track record of consistent double-digit growth over the past five years, while its focus remains on making strategic investments that support sustainable long-term value creation.

Praveen Rao Akkinepally, Country President and Managing Director, AstraZeneca Pharma India Ltd., said the company's purpose is to push the boundaries of science to deliver life-changing medicines and that this continues to shape its efforts to address unmet patient needs in India. He said the growth and momentum recorded during the quarter reflected the strength of the company's portfolio and its focus on expanding access to serve more patients across the country.

During the quarter, AstraZeneca Pharma India strengthened its portfolio through important regulatory approvals, expanded scientific engagement through targeted capability-building initiatives and advanced strategic partnerships supporting earlier diagnosis and broader access. The company said these developments reflect its continued focus on addressing unmet medical needs, strengthening its presence across priority therapy areas and creating long-term value through science, innovation and sustainable growth.

Among the key regulatory milestones, acalabrutinib received approval in combination with venetoclax, with or without obinutuzumab, for the treatment of patients with previously untreated chronic lymphocytic leukaemia (CLL)/small lymphocytic lymphoma (SLL). Acalabrutinib also received approval in combination with bendamustine and rituximab for the treatment of adult patients with previously untreated mantle cell lymphoma (MCL) who are not eligible for autologous stem cell transplant (ASCT).

The company also received regulatory approval for trastuzumab deruxtecan in combination with pertuzumab for the first-line treatment of adult patients with unresectable or metastatic HER2-positive breast cancer, defined as IHC3+ or ISH+ disease.

As part of its strategic initiatives, AstraZeneca Pharma India signed a Memorandum of Understanding with the Government of Telangana to introduce AI-enabled lung cancer screening across public healthcare facilities in the state. Under the collaboration, AstraZeneca will facilitate the deployment of Qure.ai's AI-powered chest X-ray solution to support clinicians in identifying high-risk pulmonary nodules and other lung conditions, enabling earlier triage and follow-up. The initiative is expected to be rolled out across 20 public health facilities covering urban and rural settings and will include training and upskilling of healthcare professionals to support effective and sustainable adoption.

The company also launched K+ Connect, a pan-India multidisciplinary initiative focused on advancing the management of hyperkalaemia among patients living with heart failure and chronic kidney disease. The initiative brings together clinicians from different specialties to encourage a more coordinated approach to risk identification, monitoring and management of hyperkalaemia.

Another initiative launched during the quarter was India Coronary Conquest (ICC) 2026, in collaboration with STEMI India. Described as a clinician-led national complex PCI challenge, the programme is designed to strengthen evidence-based learning and peer exchange among interventional cardiologists. It aims to support capability building in advanced cardiovascular care through case-based learning and scientific collaboration.

AstraZeneca Pharma India also received recognition during the period. At the OPPI India Awards 2026, the company received the Medical Excellence Award for its contributions to Rare Disease and was named Runner-up in the Marketing Excellence category for its Hyperkalaemia & Kidney Care initiative in Biopharmaceuticals.

At the ETHRWorld Employee Experience Awards 2026, AstraZeneca Pharma India received the Gold Award in the Exceptional Employee Experience in Driving Business Impact category, recognising the company's commitment to fostering a high-performing, collaborative and purpose-driven workplace.

AstraZeneca Pharma India Limited (AZPIL) is the listed operating company of AstraZeneca in India. The science-led biopharmaceutical company focuses on the discovery, development and commercialisation of prescription medicines across key therapy areas including Oncology, Biopharmaceuticals and Rare Disease. The company has a workforce of more than 600 employees across India and is focused on advancing innovative science, expanding access to differentiated medicines and contributing to patient care through commercial execution and partnerships across the healthcare ecosystem.
